licence: reduced values from Kitzmann and Heng 2018's compilation, the only machine-readable copy found, cited to the primary and to Kitzmann and Heng as the compiler: the measured values are the authors' facts, and the repository's GPL-3.0 covers its code and arrangement, not a reduced visible subset of one material; its compilation/readme.txt sets no separate terms for the data. No compilation file and none of LX-MIE's code is committed (decision-composition §5; decision-r08-licences.md)
reduction: n linear and k linear in log k in wavelength between the source's rows, onto 380–780 nm every 5 nm, to six significant figures; the source's rows are about 3.5–8 nm apart here. Its visible part is Khachai et al.'s first-principles (FP-APW+lo) calculation, not a measurement, so the file is a stated stand-in. The copy states no temperature. Its k, 1.46 × 10⁻² at 550 nm and 1.26–1.27 × 10⁻² over 600–780 nm with no feature, is not a colourless solid's absorption, so the file bounds the crystal's visible k from above (R08.T5.i, decision-p14-t49c-split §5.3). Its cause is not established: the ruling reads it as a computed spectrum's broadening tail or too small a computed gap, but Kitzmann and Heng took Khachai et al.'s values from a figure (their Table 1, "Data available as figure"; the arXiv copy, arXiv:1710.04946v2, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1710.04946v2, SHA-256 ba36c5a2cc6ee4dc71fbf11d461301324f1e144d3700d72f61d1ebb8e83723ec, fetched 2026-10-16), and the compilation's k stays near 1.25 × 10⁻² from 0.56 to 1.6 µm and is 8.6 × 10⁻³ at 20 µm, flat where a tail below a gap would fall, so a floor from the digitising is as likely. PubChem's Hazardous Substances Data Bank entries for sodium sulfide (CID 14804, "Color/Form", PubChem's record, https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/rest/pug_view/data/compound/14804/JSON?heading=Color/Form, SHA-256 be262d6b1122cc6f6eb45de0a7a702fbce68c931cab62497d0357819e4b26415, fetched 2026-10-16) give "CLEAR CRYSTALS; YELLOW OR BRICK-RED LUMPS OR FLAKES" (the National Fire Protection Association's Fire Protection Guide on Hazardous Materials, 7th ed., 1978), "AMORPHOUS, YELLOW-PINK OR WHITE CRYSTALS" (Sax 1979) and "White to pink, crystalline solid" (Ashford 1994), and state no cause of the coloured forms. At the file's k a 30 µm crystal would transmit 4.4 × 10⁻⁵ at 550 nm, an absorption length of 3.0 µm (computed): not clear. R08.T5.i's search (2026-10-16) found no measured visible constants of Na2S, as R08.T5.d's did not; Walker 1979 ("Crystal growth of sodium sulphide, Na2S", J. Cryst. Growth 47, 598, DOI 10.1016/0022-0248(79)90146-5; OpenAlex's record, https://api.openalex.org/works/doi:10.1016/0022-0248(79)90146-5, SHA-256 fd28561691a2125a61393da08e570208147ad1653a5ed693a84352ea0f1826e5, fetched 2026-10-16) is closed, its title alone reachable
standIn: a computed index, from a first-principles calculation of the crystal, since no measured visible optical constants were found; its flat visible k is a computed spectrum's, not a colourless solid's absorption, so it is an upper bound on the crystal's absorption
